ctor.rationale: `base(2, CardType.Skill, CardRarity.Uncommon, TargetType.AllEnemies)` (Shockwave.cs:27-30) == cost 2 / SKILL / UNCOMMON / ALL_ENEMIES. `handles_own_routing = True` (725) is faithful: C#'s OnPlay iterates HittableEnemies itself, so the sim must not let the framework call `on_play` once per enemy on top of that.

CanonicalVars.rationale: `new DynamicVar("Power", 3m)` (Shockwave.cs:17) == `_power_amount = 3`, used for BOTH debuffs. Safe collapse here because C# reads the single `Power` var for both applications (Shockwave.cs:36, 39-40) -- unlike card/prowess, where two separate C# vars happened to coincide.

OnPlay.rationale: `foreach (enemy in CombatState.HittableEnemies) { await PowerCmd.Apply<WeakPower>(...); await PowerCmd.Apply<VulnerablePower>(...); }` (Shockwave.cs:37-41) == `for enemy in [e for e in ctx.enemies if not e.is_gone]: PowerCmd.apply(WeakPower); PowerCmd.apply(VulnerablePower)`. Weak BEFORE Vulnerable per enemy, and the enemy loop is the OUTER loop on both sides, which matters for a per-application listener. `is_gone` is the right analogue of HittableEnemies here, and unlike the damage AoEs there is no per-hit fan-out question -- these are powers, so C# applies them one creature at a time too and the conflagration finding does not apply. Presentation, folded in: TriggerAnim (34), the flying-slash VFX (35) and two hover tips (21-25).
